$comment: Asks for scripts/live-turn.mjs. `ops` is what a task aims at, not a promise the model will use them; scripts/tool-report.mjs next ranks tasks by how much their ops need a run.

tasks.task: List the scenes in this project, open the main one, and tell me every node in it with its type. Then tell me the Player's position and the Label's text.
In the main scene add an Enemy node: a Node2D at position (400, 200) with a Sprite2D child named Body and a Label child that says "enemy". Save the scene and show me the resulting tree.
In the main scene, rename Ticker to Clock, move the Timer directly under Main, duplicate the Player as Player2, and save. Tell me the final tree.
Put the Player in a group called actors and the Label in a group called ui. Then take the Label out of ui again and delete it entirely. Save and confirm what groups the Player has now.
Connect the Timer's timeout signal to a method called _on_ticker_timeout on Main as a scene connection, save, and show me the connection. Then disconnect it again and save.
Turn the Player node from a Node2D into a CharacterBody2D, keeping its script and position. Save and verify the type and position afterwards.

Create a new scene at res://scenes/coin.tscn with an Area2D root named Coin and a Sprite2D child. Save it. Then open the main scene, place two instances of the coin under Main at (100, 100) and (200, 100), and save the main scene as res://scenes/main_with_coins.tscn.
Open the main scene, move the Player to (999, 999) without saving, then reload the scene from disk and tell me where the Player is now.
Rename the Label node to Title, then undo that rename, then redo it. After each step tell me the Label's current name from the scene tree.

assets/tiles.png is a 128x32 atlas of sixteen 16x16 tiles: row 0 is ground, brick, question block, spent block, pipe mouth left, pipe mouth right, pipe shaft left, pipe shaft right; row 1 is flag pole, pole ball, flag, castle brick, bush left, bush right, cloud left, cloud right. Cut it into a TileSet at res://assets/tiles.tres where ground and brick are solid, add a TileMapLayer named Ground to the main scene, paint a floor of ground tiles from x=0 to x=19 at y=10 with one brick at (5, 8), save, and read back what the layer holds.

The project has no player art. Draw a 32x32 PNG at res://assets/hero.png with a blue body and a yellow 8x8 head on a transparent background, then give the Player a Sprite2D child that shows it. Save and list the files under assets.
Save a 24x24 rectangle collision shape at res://assets/player_shape.tres, give the Player a CollisionShape2D child that uses it, and save the scene.

List every file in the project with its size. There is an old save system script nobody uses; read it to confirm nothing references it, move it into a folder called res://legacy/, then delete it and make sure the editor filesystem is up to date.

In scripts/player.gd add an exported variable jump_force of type float defaulting to 300.0, and a function jump() that prints the jump force. Make sure the file has no diagnostics afterwards and is formatted the way gdformat wants it.

Write a new script at res://scripts/coin.gd that extends Area2D, has an exported int value defaulting to 1, and prints "collected" in a _on_body_entered handler. Check it has no diagnostics, then close it.

List every function and variable declared in scripts/main.gd. Find where total_ticks is declared, and tell me what the hover documentation says for the Timer type used in that file. Then find every symbol in the whole project whose name contains tick.
In scripts/main.gd, how many places reference the _on_tick function, and on which lines? Also give me every highlight of total_ticks in that file.
In scripts/main.gd, what completions does the language server offer right after typing `timer.` at the end of _ready? And what is the signature help for the print call inside _announce?
Rename the function _announce in scripts/main.gd to _say_tick everywhere it is used, using the language server's rename so nothing is missed. Confirm there are no diagnostics afterwards.
What is this project's name, main scene, and window size? Also find every project setting whose name mentions vsync and tell me their values.
Set the project's window width to 1280 and height to 720, then read them back. Then reset the max_fps setting to its default and tell me what it was before and what it is now.
Find the editor settings about the text editor's indentation, read the indent type, set it to spaces, and read it back.

Create a script res://scripts/game_state.gd extending Node with a var score := 0, register it as an autoload named GameState, list the autoloads to confirm, then remove it again and confirm the list is empty.

Add an input action jump bound to the space key and the A gamepad button, and an action shoot bound to the left mouse button. List the actions to confirm. Then remove shoot, override ui_accept to the Enter key only, and finally reset ui_accept back to its built-in default.
Which editor plugins does this project have, and which are enabled? If any is disabled, enable it and confirm.
Run the game, take a screenshot after it has started, list the running scene tree, and stop the game. Tell me what the screenshot shows and what nodes were running.
Run the game, let it run for about 120 frames, then read the Player's travelled value and position, and the engine's FPS and object count monitors. Stop the game and report the numbers.
Run the game, pause it, confirm from the tree that it is paused, resume it, then restart it from scratch and stop it. Report each state change.

Add an input action move_right on the D key and make the Player move 100 pixels per second to the right while it is held, in scripts/player.gd. Then run the game, hold D for about half a second, and prove from the Player's position that it moved.
Run the game for about six seconds, stop it, and then tell me how many "live tick" lines the game printed and whether any warning appeared, quoting the warning.

Put a breakpoint on the line inside _on_tick that assigns total_ticks in scripts/main.gd, launch the game under the debugger, wait for it to stop, and tell me the value of ticks and total_ticks from the locals. Continue once, read them again at the next stop, then terminate.

Break on the _announce call inside _on_tick in scripts/main.gd, launch under the debugger, and when it stops: step over one line and tell me the line, then on the next stop step into _announce and tell me the frame you are in, then step out and tell me where you land. Terminate afterwards.

Launch the game under the debugger with a breakpoint on the push_warning line in scripts/main.gd. When it stops, evaluate the expressions ticks * 2 and TICK_MESSAGE, list the threads, report the adapter status, and terminate.

Launch the game under the debugger with no breakpoints, pause it after it has run for a moment, tell me what the stack trace says while paused, continue, then restart the debuggee and finally disconnect, terminating the game.
Run the game normally first. Then attach the debugger to the running game, set a breakpoint on the _announce call in scripts/main.gd, wait for it to stop, read the locals, and terminate.
For scripts/main.gd, tell me which of lines 1, 2, 12, 18 and 26 can hold a breakpoint, and set breakpoints on every one of them that can.

Using the Godot documentation, explain in three sentences what CharacterBody2D.move_and_slide does and when to call it, and quote the passage you based that on. Also list the top three documentation passages about Timer.autostart.
Report the editor session's status and engine version. Then stop the editor session, start it again, and confirm it is ready by opening the main scene.

Open the main scene and change the Label's text to "dirty" without saving. Then open scenes/main.tscn again from disk; if the editor puts up a dialog asking what to do with the unsaved changes, tell me its buttons and press the one that discards the changes.

Add a score that goes up by 10 every second, shown in a Label at the top of the screen, and print the score each time it changes. Run the game for about three seconds and prove from the log that the score rose.
This project does not run. Find out why, fix it so the game scene starts, run it to prove it, take a screenshot, and stop it.

The fighter takes far too much damage when the game runs: the scene sets armour to 10, and it still dies within seconds. Find where the damage goes wrong with the debugger rather than by guessing — a breakpoint inside take_damage and the values in its frame — fix it, and show with two health readings a few seconds apart that the fighter now survives.

In scripts/main.gd, use the language server's go-to-definition on the _on_timeout reference inside _ready and tell me the line it is defined on. Then use go-to-declaration on TICK_MESSAGE where it is used inside _announce and tell me where it is declared. Give both as line numbers and quote the lines.
Ask the Godot documentation one question and give me its answer as one paragraph with a supporting quote: what does Timer.autostart do, and does it work for a Timer added at runtime?

In scripts/main.gd, check with the language server whether the symbol total_ticks can be renamed, and tell me the range and placeholder it proposes. Do the same for the string literal "live tick". Do not rename anything.
List only the GDScript files in this project with their sizes in bytes, largest first, and tell me which one nothing else references.

Create a minimal editor plugin at res://addons/hello/: a plugin.cfg naming it Hello with script plugin.gd, and plugin.gd that is a @tool script extending EditorPlugin and prints "hello plugin" in _enter_tree. Make sure the editor sees the new files, enable the plugin, and confirm from the plugin list that Hello is enabled.

Run the game exactly as the project is now. If the editor puts up a dialog, tell me its title and buttons and dismiss it with the button that cancels. Then set the main scene to the one scene the project has and run it for real, and stop it.

Build a coin the player can collect. Draw a 16x16 yellow coin texture, make a coin scene at res://scenes/coin.tscn whose root is an Area2D with a Sprite2D and a CollisionShape2D (a 16x16 rectangle shape), and a script that prints "collected" and frees the coin when a body enters it. Turn the Player into a CharacterBody2D with its own 24x24 rectangle collision shape, and make it move 200 px/s to the right while the D key is held. Place three coins to the right of the player at x = 120, 180, 240 on the player's y. Run the game, hold D for about a second, and prove from the log that at least one coin printed "collected".

Add an Enemy node to the main scene that starts 300 px to the right of the Player and moves toward the Player at 60 px/s every frame, printing the remaining distance once per second. Run the game for about three seconds and prove with two reads of the Enemy's position that it got closer.

Make the fighter script crash on purpose: at the third tick, index an empty array. Launch the game under the debugger with no breakpoints, wait for the debugger to stop on the error, and report the stack frame, the line, and the value of ticks from the locals. Then remove the crash again, launch once more, let it run two seconds without stopping, and terminate.

Make the player a platformer character. Cut assets/tiles.png (16x16 tiles, 8 across, 2 down; the top-left tile is ground) into a TileSet where the ground tile is solid, paint a floor of ground from x=0 to x=39 at y=14 on a TileMapLayer, turn the Player into a CharacterBody2D with a 16x24 rectangle collision shape placed on top of the floor, give it gravity and a jump on the Space key (a new input action named jump), save, run the game, wait until it has landed, press Space, and prove with two position reads that it went up and came back down.

Add a Score label at the top left of the main scene and a script on Main that keeps an integer score. Every time the Timer ticks, the score goes up by 5 and the label shows it. Wire the Timer's timeout to the handler as a scene connection rather than in code. Run the game for about three seconds and prove from the label's text that the score rose.

Add a pause menu: pressing Escape toggles the scene tree's paused state and shows a Label saying PAUSED in the middle of the screen; pressing it again hides the label and resumes. Bind Escape to a new input action named pause_game. Run the game, press Escape once, prove from the running tree that it is paused and the label is visible, press it again, and prove it resumed.

Make the Player fire a bullet every half second: a bullet scene at res://scenes/bullet.tscn (Node2D root with a small ColorRect) whose script moves it right at 400 px/s and frees it once its x passes 700, printing "bullet gone". Instantiate bullets from player.gd under Main using a Timer. Run the game for about three seconds and prove with the running tree and the log that bullets were spawned and freed.

Rename scripts/player.gd to scripts/hero.gd and keep the game working: the Player node must still use it, and whatever referenced the old path must point at the new one. Prove it by running the game for two seconds and reading the log for errors, then stop it.

Make two levels: res://scenes/level_a.tscn and res://scenes/level_b.tscn, each a Node2D root with a Label naming the level. Make the main scene start by loading level_a under a node named LevelHolder, and switch to level_b when the N key is pressed (a new input action next_level). Run the game, read the tree to prove level_a is loaded, press N, and prove level_b replaced it.

In scripts/player.gd, on ready, tween the Player from its start position to (400, 200) over two seconds. Run the game, read the Player's position at about half a second and again at about two and a half seconds, and prove it moved and then stopped at the target.

Give the Player a Camera2D child that is the current camera, and make the Player move right at 300 px/s while the D key is held. Run the game, hold D for a second, and prove with the camera's global position before and after that the camera followed the player.

Make the game save the total tick count to user://ticks.json every tick and print "saved N" each time, and on start load the file if it exists and print "loaded N". Run the game for three seconds, stop it, run it again for two seconds, and prove from the log that the second run loaded the count the first run saved.

Add an AnimationPlayer to the main scene with an animation named fade that takes the Label's modulate alpha from 1 to 0 over one second, and play it on ready. Run the game, read the Label's modulate at about half a second and again after the animation is over, and prove it faded.

Declare a custom signal tick_reached(count) on Main that is emitted from _on_tick, and add a Counter node with its own script that connects to that signal in code and prints "counter saw N". Run the game for three seconds and prove from the log that Counter saw ticks 1, 2 and 3.

Cut assets/tiles.png (16x16 tiles, 8 across, 2 down, top-left is ground and the one right of it is brick) into a solid TileSet, paint a floor of ground at y=14 from x=0 to x=30 and a wall of brick at x=12 from y=10 to y=13. Make the Player a CharacterBody2D standing on the floor at x=64 with a 14x22 rectangle shape, moving right at 150 px/s while D is held. Run the game, hold D for three seconds, and prove with the Player's position that it stopped at the wall instead of passing through it.

Create a res://scenes/npc.tscn whose root is a Node2D with an exported String property display_name and a Label child that shows it on ready. Place three NPC instances in the main scene named Bob, Alice and Kim with display_name set to their names. Run the game and prove from the running nodes that each Label shows the right name.

Add a jump() function to scripts/player.gd that sets a jumped flag and prints "jumped", called when a new input action jump (Space) is just pressed. Launch the game under the debugger with a breakpoint on the print inside jump(), press Space so it fires, and when it stops report the stack frames and the value of jumped. Then continue and terminate.

Launch the pipeline game under the debugger with a breakpoint on the return line of _floor_damage in scripts/fighter.gd. When it stops, report every frame on the stack, the value of amount in the top frame, the value of after_resistance in the take_damage frame below it, and evaluate minimum_damage * 2. Step out once and say which frame you are in. Terminate.

Run the game and attach the debugger while it keeps running. Evaluate total_ticks in the running game and tell me what came back. If the debugger cannot answer while the game runs, get the value the way it can, then disconnect and stop the game.

Rewrite scripts/player.gd as a whole new file rather than editing lines: keep what it does, but call the distance variable distance instead of travelled and make speed default to 48.0. Check the diagnostics, then run the game for a second and read the distance to prove it moves.

This game breaks the moment it starts. Run it, find out from the editor what breaks and where, fix the script so it starts cleanly, and run it again to prove the Player moves for two seconds. Then stop it.
Add a HUD to the main scene: a health bar, the score and a minimap.
Make a title screen scene for this game that uses the art in assets/, and make it the scene the game starts on.
